2º de Bachillerato · Inglés II

Linking words and connectors

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

«Despite it was raining, we went out» es un error muy común. ¿Qué falla, si «despite» significa «a pesar de»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Despite es una preposición: va seguida de un sustantivo o de un -ing, no de una oración con sujeto y verbo. Las versiones correctas son Despite the rain, we went out, Despite it raining… o Despite the fact that it was raining… Si quieres una oración completa, necesitas una conjunción: Although it was raining, we went out. Cada conector tiene su gramática y su puntuación, y eso es lo que se evalúa en la PAU.

2

Aprende12 apartados

Para empezar: Should homework be banned?

Homework has been part of school life for over a century. However, more and more parents and teachers are questioning its value. Some countries, such as Finland, give students very little homework, and yet their results are among the best in the world.

On the one hand, homework helps students to practise what they have learnt and, moreover, it teaches them to organise their time. Furthermore, it allows parents to see what their children are doing at school. On the other hand, too much homework can cause stress and, as a result, students may lose interest in learning. In addition, not all families can help their children, which means that homework may increase inequality.

In my opinion, homework should not be banned altogether. Nevertheless, it should be short and meaningful so that students still have time to rest, play sports and spend time with their families. All in all, the question is not whether to give homework, but how much and what kind.

El texto es un ensayo de opinión breve. Fíjate en cómo los conectores (however, moreover, as a result, nevertheless, all in all) guían al lector de una idea a otra.

8.1 Qué hacen los conectores y cómo se puntúan

Los conectores (linking words) relacionan ideas: añaden, contrastan, explican causas, extraen consecuencias u ordenan. Un texto con buenos conectores tiene cohesión, y el lector sigue el razonamiento sin esfuerzo. En la PAU, la cohesión es uno de los criterios de corrección del writing.

Gramaticalmente hay tres grupos, y cada uno se puntúa de una manera distinta:

TipoEjemplosPuntuación
Conjunciones coordinantesand, but, or, so, yetunen dos oraciones en una: I was tired, but I went out.
Conjunciones subordinantesalthough, because, while, whereas, so that, unlessintroducen una oración; si van delante, coma: Although I was tired, I went out.
Adverbios conectoreshowever, therefore, moreover, neverthelessempiezan oración nueva o van tras punto y coma, con coma: I was tired. However, I went out.
Preposicionesdespite, because of, due to, in addition to+ sustantivo o -ing: Despite being tired, …

El error más frecuente es usar un adverbio como si fuera una conjunción: *I was tired, however I went out. Debe ser I was tired. However, I went out o I was tired; however, I went out.

8.2 Adición

Para añadir información, de lo más sencillo a lo más formal: and, also, too, as well (informales), in addition, furthermore, moreover, what is more, besides (formales, al principio de la oración y seguidos de coma).

Also va antes del verbo principal y después de be o del auxiliar: She also speaks French. He is also a writer. Too y as well van al final: She speaks French too / as well.

In addition to y besides también pueden ser preposiciones, seguidas de sustantivo o de -ing: In addition to studying, she works part-time. Besides being cheap, it's healthy.

Not only… but (also) añade con énfasis: Cycling is not only cheap but also good for your health. Al principio de la frase exige inversión (tema 9): Not only is cycling cheap, but it is also healthy. Otras parejas: both… and (both young and old people), as well as (She plays the piano as well as the guitar).

En un ensayo, no empieces todos los párrafos con el mismo conector: alterna Firstly… In addition… Furthermore… Finally…

8.3 Contraste y concesión con conjunciones

But y yet unen dos oraciones opuestas: It's expensive, but it's worth it. Yet es algo más formal y sorprendente: He's rich, yet he lives very simply.

Although, though y even though introducen una concesión (un obstáculo que no impide el resultado) con sujeto y verbo: Although it was late, we kept working. Even though she had studied, she failed (más enfático). Though es más informal y puede ir al final: It was cold. We went out, though.

While y whereas comparan dos hechos opuestos, a menudo de dos sujetos distintos: My brother loves football, whereas I prefer tennis. While some people enjoy city life, others need nature. While también puede ser concesivo al principio: While I understand your point, I disagree.

No mezcles conectores: *Although it was raining, but we went out es un calco del español. Basta con uno: Although it was raining, we went out o It was raining, but we went out.

Vídeo: Though, although, even though, despite, in spite of · Adam's English Lessons · engVid (YouTube) · 3,7 millones de visualizaciones

8.4 Contraste con adverbios y preposiciones: however, despite

However, nevertheless, nonetheless y even so son adverbios: empiezan una oración nueva y van seguidos de coma. The plan is expensive. However, it will create jobs. The team played badly. Nevertheless, they won. However también puede ir en medio, entre comas: The plan, however, has some problems.

On the other hand presenta el otro lado de un argumento (suele ir después de on the one hand). On the contrary niega lo anterior y afirma lo opuesto: The film wasn't boring. On the contrary, it was fascinating. No los confundas.

Despite e in spite of son preposiciones, seguidas de sustantivo, -ing o the fact that + oración: Despite the rain, we went out. In spite of feeling ill, she came to work. Despite the fact that he was injured, he finished the race. Nunca *despite of ni *despite it was.

Reescritura clásica de la PAU: Although he was very tired, he went to the party → Despite being very tired, he went to the party / In spite of his tiredness… / Despite the fact that he was very tired…

Vídeo: How to express opposing ideas: despite, although, nevertheless · English with Emma · engVid (YouTube) · 2 millones de visualizaciones

8.5 Causa

Con conjunciones + oración: because, as, since. We stayed in because it was raining. As y since suelen ir al principio y presentan una causa conocida: As it was late, we took a taxi. Since you're here, you can help me.

Con preposiciones + sustantivo o -ing: because of, due to, owing to, on account of, as a result of, thanks to (causa positiva). The match was cancelled because of the rain. The delay was due to a technical problem. Owing to bad weather, the flight was diverted.

Due to va tradicionalmente detrás de be (The delay was due to…), y owing to al principio de la frase; hoy ambos se usan casi igual, pero en un writing formal es más elegante respetar esa diferencia.

Con the fact that se puede convertir una preposición en conjunción: Due to the fact that prices have risen, sales have fallen.

Reescritura típica: The flight was delayed because the weather was bad → The flight was delayed because of / due to the bad weather.

8.6 Consecuencia y resultado

So une dos oraciones (coma delante): It was late, so we took a taxi. En registro formal se usan adverbios: therefore, consequently, as a result, as a consequence, thus, hence. Prices have risen. As a result, many families are struggling. The road was closed; therefore, we had to take a detour.

Therefore puede ir también en medio, tras el sujeto o el auxiliar: The evidence is, therefore, inconclusive. Hence puede ir seguido de un sustantivo: The weather was terrible, hence the delay.

Para expresar una consecuencia con intensidad: so + adjetivo / adverbio + that y such (a) + (adjetivo +) sustantivo + that. The film was so boring that we left. It was such a boring film that we left. There were so many people that we couldn't get in. She has such good taste.

Error típico: *It was so a boring film o *It was such boring. Recuerda: so + adjetivo solo; such + sustantivo (con o sin adjetivo).

Which means that y leading to son muy útiles en los ensayos para encadenar consecuencias: Rents have doubled, which means that young people cannot leave home.

8.7 Finalidad

Cuando el sujeto es el mismo, la finalidad se expresa con to + base, in order to o so as to (estos dos, más formales): I went to Dublin to improve my English. The government has raised taxes in order to reduce the deficit. En negativa se usa in order not to o so as not to: I left early so as not to miss the bus (no *to not miss en registro formal).

So that + sujeto + modal (can, could, will, would) se usa sobre todo cuando cambia el sujeto: I'll explain it again so that everyone understands. She spoke slowly so that we could follow her. I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget.

For + sustantivo expresa finalidad (We went out for a walk) y for + -ing describe la función de un objeto: This knife is for cutting bread. Pero nunca *for + infinitivo ni *for + -ing con el propósito de una persona: *I came here for to study / for studying → I came here to study.

Reescritura típica: I took a map because I didn't want to get lost → I took a map so as not to get lost / so that I wouldn't get lost / in case I got lost (precaución).

8.8 Tiempo y orden del discurso

Para ordenar pasos o argumentos: first(ly), to begin with, second(ly), next, then, after that, finally, lastly. En una narración: at first, then, later, afterwards, in the end, eventually.

Pares que se confunden: at first (al principio, en contraste con después) frente a first (primero, en una secuencia); in the end / eventually (finalmente, después de mucho tiempo o dificultades) frente a at last (por fin, con alivio) y at the end of + sustantivo (al final de algo): At first I hated it, but in the end I loved it. At last you're here! At the end of the film, everyone cried.

Conjunciones de tiempo: when, while, as, as soon as, once, until, before, after, by the time, since. Recuerda que con futuro llevan presente: Once you've finished, you can leave. As soon as I get home, I'll call you. Meanwhile / in the meantime son adverbios: Dinner will be ready in an hour. Meanwhile, let's tidy up.

En la PAU, los conectores de secuencia ayudan a responder preguntas de orden de los hechos y a estructurar la parte narrativa de un writing.

8.9 Ejemplos, aclaraciones y énfasis

Para dar ejemplos: for example, for instance (adverbios, con coma), such as y like (+ sustantivo, sin coma detrás). Some sports, such as tennis and golf, are expensive. Many cities, for instance Paris and Rome, have banned old cars. No se dice *such as for example.

Para aclarar o reformular: that is (to say), in other words, namely, i.e. (= that is), e.g. (= for example). Only one student, namely Ana, passed. The project failed; in other words, we wasted a lot of money.

Para enfatizar o precisar: in fact, indeed, actually, especially, particularly, in particular, above all. The results were good. In fact, they were the best in years. Young people, especially those in big cities, struggle to find housing.

Cuidado con los falsos amigos: actually significa «en realidad», no «actualmente» (currently, nowadays); y eventually significa «finalmente», no «eventualmente».

8.10 Opinión y actitud

Para dar una opinión: In my opinion / view, …; I believe / feel that…; As far as I'm concerned, …; From my point of view, …; It seems to me that…; Personally, … No se dice *In my opinion, I think… (es redundante) ni *According to me (according to se usa para fuentes ajenas: according to the report).

Para presentar opiniones ajenas: It is often said / argued that…; Some people claim that…; Critics point out that…; Supporters of… believe that…

Los adverbios de actitud muestran la postura del autor y son clave en la comprensión lectora: clearly, obviously, undoubtedly (certeza), apparently, presumably (duda), fortunately, unfortunately, surprisingly, sadly (valoración), admittedly (reconozco que), ideally, hopefully.

Admittedly es muy útil para la concesión en un ensayo: Admittedly, electric cars are expensive. However, they save money in the long term. Esta estructura (concesión + contraargumento) demuestra capacidad de argumentar.

Vídeo: Palabras y frases de transición para mejorar tu escritura · 7ESL Learning English (YouTube) · 1,6 millones de visualizaciones

8.11 Concluir y resumir

La conclusión de un ensayo empieza con un conector que avisa al lector: In conclusion, …; To conclude, …; To sum up, …; All in all, …; On balance, …; Overall, …; Taking everything into account, …

On balance y taking everything into account son especialmente buenos para los ensayos de ventajas e inconvenientes (for and against), porque indican que se han sopesado ambos lados: On balance, the benefits of tourism outweigh its drawbacks.

Evita conectores demasiado coloquiales (So, basically, …; Anyway, …) y el calco *In conclusion, to finish. Tampoco conviene introducir argumentos nuevos en la conclusión: resume, da tu opinión final y, si quieres, termina con una recomendación o una pregunta.

Modelo: All in all, although homework has some advantages, I believe it should be limited so that students can enjoy a balanced life. Una sola frase como esta, con tres conectores de distinto tipo, demuestra mucho nivel.

8.12 Los conectores en la PAU

En las reescrituras se pide cambiar un conector por otro sin cambiar el significado, lo que obliga a cambiar también la estructura:

OriginalReescritura
Although it was cold, we swam.Despite the cold / it being cold, we swam.
He was late because the traffic was heavy.He was late because of / due to the heavy traffic.
It was such a hard exam that nobody passed.The exam was so hard that nobody passed.
She studied hard. She wanted to pass.She studied hard in order to / so as to pass.
I'll repeat it. I want everyone to understand.I'll repeat it so that everyone understands.
He's rich. However, he isn't happy.Although he's rich, he isn't happy.

Método: 1) identifica la relación lógica (contraste, causa, finalidad…); 2) mira la categoría del nuevo conector (¿va con oración, con sustantivo o con -ing?); 3) adapta la estructura y la puntuación.

En el writing, la corrección valora la variedad y el uso correcto de los conectores. Una buena técnica es preparar un «kit» de diez conectores de distinto tipo y practicar con ellos hasta usarlos sin errores.

Vídeo: 15 conectores para escribir un essay en inglés (B2, C1, EBAU) · Inglés Para Perezosos (YouTube) · 319 mil visualizaciones

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Reescribe con despite: «Although she was ill, she went to school.»

  1. Despite es preposición: no admite oración.
  2. Despite + -ing (mismo sujeto) o + the fact that.

Resultado: Despite being ill, she went to school / Despite the fact that she was ill, she went to school.

Ejemplo 2. Corrige la puntuación: «The hotel was cheap, however it was dirty.»

  1. However es un adverbio, no una conjunción.
  2. Punto o punto y coma delante y coma detrás.

Resultado: The hotel was cheap. However, it was dirty / The hotel was cheap; however, it was dirty.

Ejemplo 3. Reescribe con due to: «The match was cancelled because it was snowing heavily.»

  1. Due to + sustantivo.
  2. Convertir la oración en un sintagma nominal.

Resultado: The match was cancelled due to the heavy snow.

Ejemplo 4. Reescribe con such: «The concert was so good that we didn't want to leave.»

  1. Such + (a) + adjetivo + sustantivo.
  2. Concert es contable singular: such a.

Resultado: It was such a good concert that we didn't want to leave.

Ejemplo 5. Une con so that: «I'm saving money. I want to travel next summer.»

  1. Finalidad con modal.
  2. Mismo sujeto: so that I can (también to / in order to).

Resultado: I'm saving money so that I can travel next summer.

Ejemplo 6. Une con whereas: «My sister is very sociable. I am quite shy.»

  1. Comparación de dos hechos opuestos.
  2. Whereas une las dos oraciones con coma.

Resultado: My sister is very sociable, whereas I am quite shy.

Errores típicos

  • Usar despite con oración: *Despite it was cold → Despite the cold / Although it was cold.
  • Puntuar however como conjunción: *It was cheap, however it was bad → It was cheap. However, it was bad.
  • Duplicar conectores: *Although it rained, but we went → Although it rained, we went.
  • Decir despite of: *despite of the rain → despite the rain / in spite of the rain.
  • Confundir so y such: *It was so a nice day → It was such a nice day.
  • Usar for + infinitivo para la finalidad: *I study for to pass → I study to pass.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (32)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Completa con but o although: «___ it was expensive, we bought it.»

    Ver solución
    Although: conjunción subordinante al principio.

  2. Completa con because o because of: «We stayed at home ___ the storm.»

    Ver solución
    because of: + sustantivo.

  3. Completa: «The film was ___ boring that I fell asleep.»

    Ver solución
    so: so + adjetivo + that.

  4. Completa: «It was ___ a long day that I went to bed at nine.»

    Ver solución
    such: such a + adjetivo + sustantivo.

  5. Completa: «I went to the library ___ study.» (finalidad)

    Ver solución
    to (o in order to).

  6. Completa con however o although: «He trained hard. ___, he lost the race.»

    Ver solución
    However: inicio de oración nueva.

  7. Completa: «Some fruits, ___ oranges and lemons, are rich in vitamin C.»

    Ver solución
    such as: + sustantivos.

  8. Completa: «I like coffee, ___ my brother prefers tea.»

    Ver solución
    whereas (o while): contraste entre dos sujetos.

  9. Completa: «___ my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea.»

    Ver solución
    In: in my opinion.

  10. Completa: «___ conclusion, there are more advantages than disadvantages.»

    Ver solución
    In: in conclusion.

  11. Corrige: «Despite of the rain, we played.»

    Ver solución
    Despite the rain (o In spite of the rain), we played.

  12. Completa: «She not only sings ___ also plays the guitar.»

    Ver solución
    but: not only… but also.

Nivel medio

  1. Reescribe con in spite of: «Although he had a broken arm, he finished the race.»

    Ver solución
    In spite of having a broken arm (In spite of his broken arm), he finished the race.

  2. Reescribe con although: «Despite the bad reviews, the film was a success.»

    Ver solución
    Although the reviews were bad, the film was a success.

  3. Reescribe con due to: «The train was late because there was a technical problem.»

    Ver solución
    The train was late due to a technical problem.

  4. Reescribe con as a result: «Prices went up, so sales fell.»

    Ver solución
    Prices went up. As a result, sales fell.

  5. Reescribe con so as not to: «I whispered because I didn't want to wake the baby.»

    Ver solución
    I whispered so as not to wake the baby.

  6. Reescribe con so that: «She gave me her number. She wanted me to call her.»

    Ver solución
    She gave me her number so that I could call her.

  7. Completa con at last, in the end o at the end: «___ of the race she was exhausted, but ___ she won. ___ a medal!, her coach shouted.»

    Ver solución
    At the end; in the end (eventually); At last.

  8. Explica la diferencia: «on the other hand» / «on the contrary».

    Ver solución
    On the other hand presenta otra cara del tema; on the contrary niega lo anterior y afirma lo opuesto.

  9. Corrige: «Actually, more people work from home than ten years ago.» (quieres decir «actualmente»)

    Ver solución
    Nowadays / Currently, more people work from home than ten years ago: actually significa «en realidad».

  10. Reescribe con not only… but also: «The new phone is cheaper. It's also faster.»

    Ver solución
    The new phone is not only cheaper but also faster.

  11. Reescribe con so + adjetivo: «It was such a difficult test that nobody finished it.»

    Ver solución
    The test was so difficult that nobody finished it.

  12. Une con which means that: «Rents have doubled. Young people can't leave home.»

    Ver solución
    Rents have doubled, which means that young people can't leave home.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Reescribe con despite the fact that: «He is very rich, but he lives in a small flat.»

    Ver solución
    Despite the fact that he is very rich, he lives in a small flat.

  2. Reescribe con owing to: «The concert was postponed because the singer was ill.»

    Ver solución
    Owing to the singer's illness, the concert was postponed.

  3. Reescribe con not only al principio (inversión): «Electric cars are quiet and they don't pollute.»

    Ver solución
    Not only are electric cars quiet, but they also don't pollute (they are also non-polluting).

  4. Escribe una frase de ensayo con admittedly + however sobre las redes sociales.

    Ver solución
    Modelo: Admittedly, social media helps us stay in touch with friends. However, it can also make us feel lonely and anxious.

  5. Mejora la cohesión: «Tourism creates jobs. Tourism brings money. Tourism damages the environment. Rents go up.»

    Ver solución
    Modelo: Tourism not only creates jobs but also brings money to the area. However, it can damage the environment and, as a result, local rents tend to rise.

  6. Corrige los cinco errores: «Although it was late, but we went out. Despite it was raining, we walked. The museum was closed, however we saw the gardens. It was so a nice day. I came here for learn English.»

    Ver solución
    Although it was late, we went out; Despite the rain / Although it was raining, we walked; The museum was closed. However, we saw…; It was such a nice day; I came here to learn English.

  7. Escribe la conclusión de un ensayo sobre el uso del móvil en clase con on balance, although y so that.

    Ver solución
    Modelo: On balance, although mobile phones can be useful for some activities, I believe they should be kept in students' bags so that they can concentrate on the lesson.

  8. Escribe un párrafo de 70 palabras sobre las ventajas e inconvenientes de vivir en una gran ciudad con seis conectores de tipos distintos.

    Ver solución
    Modelo: Living in a big city has many advantages. Firstly, there are more job opportunities. Moreover, public transport is usually excellent. However, cities can be noisy and polluted. In addition, housing is so expensive that many young people cannot afford it. Therefore, although cities are exciting, they are not suitable for everyone.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeThe great school debate

El consejo de delegados quiere conocer la opinión del alumnado sobre una propuesta (semana de cuatro días, prohibir móviles, uniformes…). Cada alumno escribirá un ensayo de opinión en inglés y el grupo preparará un debate con los mejores argumentos.

Pasos

  1. Elegid la propuesta y haced una lluvia de ideas a favor y en contra.
  2. Organizad los argumentos en una tabla y asignad a cada uno un conector adecuado.
  3. Escribid un ensayo de 150 palabras con introducción, dos párrafos y conclusión, con al menos diez conectores de tipos distintos.
  4. Intercambiad los ensayos y revisad conectores y puntuación con la lista del tema.
  5. Celebrad el debate usando los conectores también en la expresión oral.

Producto final: Ensayo de opinión y participación en el debate de clase.

Cómo se valora

  • Usa conectores variados de adición, contraste, causa, consecuencia y conclusión.
  • La gramática y la puntuación de cada conector son correctas.
  • El ensayo está bien organizado y es coherente.
  • En el debate, enlaza ideas con fluidez y responde a los argumentos contrarios.

Glosario

Linking word
Conector: relaciona ideas dentro de un texto.
Cohesion
Cohesión: conexión clara entre las partes de un texto.
Conjunction
Conjunción: une oraciones (although, because).
Sentence adverb
Adverbio conector: however, therefore.
Concession
Concesión: obstáculo que no impide el resultado.
Although
Aunque (+ oración).
Despite / in spite of
A pesar de (+ sustantivo o -ing).
Whereas
Mientras que (contraste).
Due to / owing to
Debido a (+ sustantivo).
Therefore
Por tanto.
So that
Para que (+ sujeto + modal).
So as to / in order to
Para (mismo sujeto, formal).
Eventually
Finalmente (no «eventualmente»).
Admittedly
Hay que reconocer que…
On balance
Sopesándolo todo.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Comentad en inglés una noticia con «On the one hand… on the other hand…».
  • Jugad a completar frases con conectores: «I like summer although…».
  • Leed juntos un artículo de opinión en inglés y subrayad los conectores.
  • Repasad las tarjetas del tema cada noche durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Saberes básicos de Lengua Extranjera II (Inglés) de 2º de Bachillerato (RD 243/2022, BOE-A-2022-5521, bloques A. Comunicación, B. Plurilingüismo y C. Interculturalidad; en Cataluña, Decret 171/2022, Llengua Estrangera II), con la mirada puesta en la prueba de acceso a la universidad (PAU): estrategias de cohesión y coherencia textual; conectores y marcadores del discurso de adición, contraste, concesión, causa, consecuencia, finalidad, tiempo, ejemplificación, reformulación, énfasis, opinión y conclusión; diferencias gramaticales entre conjunciones, adverbios conectores y preposiciones; puntuación asociada; organización del texto argumentativo.

  • Puzle de párrafos: ordenar un ensayo desordenado guiándose por los conectores.
  • Debate con tarjetas de conectores que hay que usar antes de que acabe el turno.
  • Reescritura en cadena: cambiar el conector de una frase y adaptar la estructura.
  • Corrección colectiva de errores de puntuación con however y therefore.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Entender cómo los conectores dan cohesión a un texto y cómo se puntúan según su tipo
  • Expresar adición, contraste y concesión con la estructura correcta (although, despite, however, whereas)
  • Expresar causa, consecuencia y finalidad (because of, due to, therefore, so that, in order to)
  • Ordenar ideas en el tiempo y en el discurso, poner ejemplos, aclarar y enfatizar
  • Introducir opiniones, actitudes y conclusiones en un ensayo
  • Resolver las reescrituras con conectores de la PAU y escribir textos bien cohesionados

Palabras clave

moreover / furthermore · not only… but also · although / even though · despite / in spite of · however / nevertheless · while / whereas · because of / due to · therefore / as a result · so that / in order to · eventually / at last · such as / namely · in conclusion / on balance

Tiempo

110 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
